name: registry-stall
definition: Whether any register (foreknown/snapshots, foreknown/reaction/snapshots, darkocean/snapshots) has committed a manifest.json dated the immediately-preceding UTC day. Distinct from every source-outage signal already recorded (GDACS/NHC/FTS failures in run.json, the DMA outage in darkocean readings, the reaction axis's 'not published yet' retries) because those all presuppose the notary job reached the point of writing a manifest and committing it -- this sensor instead asks whether the job got that far at all, which none of the existing per-source checks can see from inside a run that never committed. obs-2026-08-11-1 found exactly this blind spot: verify.py's check_anchors (added 2026-08-09) makes every sentinel and darkocean run fail at the pre-commit verify step, so no failure was ever recorded as a source outage, a resolver failure, or an autonomy/log.jsonl entry of any kind -- the only trace was the absence of new snapshot directories and two 'failure' conclusions visible in GitHub's own Actions history, neither of which this repository's committed records surface on their own.
test_rule: On each nightly run, before doing anything else, compare 'yesterday' (UTC) against the newest date directory under each register's snapshots/ tree that is already committed on main. If any register's newest committed date is more than 1 day behind yesterday, record {register, newest_committed_date, days_behind} in that night's run summary. Because the failure mode this sensor targets (obs-2026-08-11-1) prevents the run from committing anything at all, the check itself must live somewhere that runs and is recorded independently of the commit gate it is watching -- e.g. a step that runs and logs to autonomy/log.jsonl even when 'Verify provenance chain' fails later in the same job (`if: always()`, matching the pattern darkocean.yml already uses for its continuity probe), or a separate always-succeeding job that only reads git history and never writes registers. The sensor fires the first night any register is more than 1 day behind, since (per obs-2026-08-11-1) this specific failure mode does not self-correct -- it recurs identically every night until a human changes the gating logic or the workflow order.
falsification: Falsified as a standing need once whatever replaces or fixes check_anchors makes a night's own fresh manifest satisfiable within the same job that writes it (e.g. anchoring happens before the verify step, or check_anchors is scoped to exclude the manifest the current job is itself producing) -- at that point a stall would again mean a genuine source or infrastructure outage worth a human's attention, not a guaranteed-permanent deadlock, and this sensor's test_rule would need reworking rather than just re-tuning its threshold. Also falsified if a register is allowed to legitimately skip a night by design (e.g. a deliberate pause) -- the sensor would need an explicit allowlist for that case rather than firing on every gap.
